implementationFollowUp.contract:
# Node test runner budget experiment

2026-10-20, macOS arm64, Node 26.5.0, shared dirty checkout. User outcome: bound resource use of Node script-test groups while preserving all test selections and behavior. Primary metric: sampled descendant-tree peak RSS; wall time/process count and test outcomes are guardrails.

Fix fixture drift first, identically for both policies. Compare the complete existing build script-test selection at Node default concurrency versus a portable wrapper capped at two by default (one on a single available CPU). CLI and NODE_TEST_CONCURRENCY overrides must preserve Node validation and test selectors. Use fresh processes, warm existing caches, no cache deletion, one warmup per policy, three alternating samples per policy for these high-cost complete groups; report median/MAD and ranges. A separate ten-pair repeat of the prior three fixture files can resolve short-workload noise if warranted.

Accept a resource governance policy for its deterministic worker bound, independent of speed claims. Claim measured full-lane resource improvement only if median RSS improves at least 15 percent and exceeds twice the larger MAD. Report wall-time regression explicitly; no blanket throughput claim. Missing dependencies/baseline failures remain visible; no assertions removed.

Also run the complete bounded gates group and CI script group after wiring. Retain cargo preparation in the CI command; inspect execution costs before running and bound task-owned processes. Signal/exit forwarding, argument precedence and real runner fan-out must have focused regression checks. No coverage, real provider calls, application/native build, or production import/reset changes. Allowed mutations: owned test fixes, a dedicated Node runner and tests, package script entry points, evidence reports and ignored logs.
